## Automation and wiring (§20.E)
- No new script. The change extends the existing standalone stall loop in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (`for ((c_idx=0; ...))`, from about line 24893 on `main`).
- Entry point: the existing scheduled poller, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` (cron / dispatch). That workflow needs no edit and stages no new files.
- No new long-running supervisor. The poller tick is the supervisor.
- No database work.
- Nothing is added to `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`, because no single-use or long-running script is introduced.

## How the clarification answers are applied
- **AD-1 = A.** The detection goes inside the existing standalone stall loop. The first miss posts a `/reclarify` comment with a marker instead of `auto_respond_clarify`. The second miss uses the existing `escalate_human` arm. The threshold stays the existing `STALL_THRESHOLD_CLARIFICATION_MINUTES` (built-in default 60 in `DEFAULT_PHASE_STALL_THRESHOLDS`). There is no new 6-hour variable; an operator who wants 6 hours sets the existing variable to 360.
- **AD-2 = A.** Security-dependency holds stay in place. The poller posts one advisory comment per (issue, dependency) pair, with the marker `<!-- ai:security-dependency-held:<issue>:<depends_on> -->`. It posts only when the comment history it already has is complete. The comment never starts with `/reclarify` and never carries the clarification-questions marker.

## Functions or modules to implement

1. **New helper `_standalone_clarify_no_output_state`** in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, placed next to `_staged_support_comments_for_guard` (about line 18924).
   - Arguments: `issue_num`, `comments_json`. The comments must be the complete history.
   - It prints one token: `has_output`, `no_output_unmarked`, or `no_output_marked <marker_epoch>`.
   - Trusted author: a login ending in `[bot]`, or `author_association` of OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR. This is the same list `stall_recovery_clarify_answer` uses (about line 26286).
   - "Clarify output" means a trusted comment whose body matches `<!-- ai:clarification-questions -->` or `^Clarification required`, or a trusted comment with a line starting `/answer`. The second form covers `/answer [auto-answered-by-clarify]` and human answers.
   - "Marker" means a trusted comment whose body starts with `"/reclarify\n<!-- ai:clarify-no-output-rerun:<issue_num> -->"`. This is the same `startswith` shape as the `security-dependency-released` check (about line 24966).
   - `marker_epoch` is the newest marker's `created_at`, read with `fromdateiso8601`. If the timestamp cannot be parsed, it is `0`, which counts as old, so escalation is never blocked forever.
   - If jq fails, the helper prints `has_output`, which keeps the existing behaviour (fail open to the legacy path).

2. **Action override in the standalone loop.** It goes right after the action is chosen (the `if recovery_count >= ...; elif ENABLE_STALL_JUDGE ...; else action=$(recovery_action_for_phase ...)` block) and before the `[standalone-stall] ... Action:` echo.
   - Reset `_std_clarify_no_output_rerun="false"` at the start of each iteration (a new local; the name is checked unused).
   - The override applies only when `phase == "ai:clarification"` and `action != "skip"`, so the per-issue and per-phase recovery caps still apply.
   - **Get complete comments:**
     - If `_standalone_staged_support_cache_available` is `complete`, use `comments_json` as it is.
     - If it is `true`, call `_staged_support_comments_for_guard "${issue_num}" "${comments_json}" "true"`. This returns the cache unchanged when there are fewer than 100 comments, and pages through the history only otherwise, so there are no new calls in the common case.
     - Otherwise, or if that fetch fails, make no override. Emit `::warning::[standalone-stall] clarify-output check skipped for issue #N: comment history incomplete` and keep the legacy action. Absence is never inferred from a partial history.
   - **Map the helper's result:**
     - `has_output`: no change. The legacy `auto_respond_clarify` or stall judge runs.
     - `no_output_unmarked`: echo `STALL_RECOVERY issue=N reason=clarify_no_output phase=ai:clarification action=retrigger_pipeline override_from=<action>`, then set `action="retrigger_pipeline"` and `_std_clarify_no_output_rerun="true"`.
     - `no_output_marked <epoch>`: if `now - epoch < threshold_minutes*60`, echo `STALL_SKIP issue=N reason=clarify_no_output_rerun_pending phase=ai:clarification action=none`, write the state as the other skips do, and `continue`. Otherwise echo `STALL_RECOVERY issue=N reason=clarify_no_output_second_miss phase=ai:clarification action=escalate_human override_from=<action>` and set `action="escalate_human"`.
   - Because the override happens before `issue_has_active_workflow`, the merged-PR guards, the fresh-push guard, zombie cancel and `phase_cap_can_dispatch`, all of those still gate the overridden action. This covers "no clarify run in progress".

3. **`retrigger_pipeline)` arm** (about line 25601). When `_std_clarify_no_output_rerun == "true"`, post this body instead of the fixed heredoc:
   ```
   /reclarify
   <!-- ai:clarify-no-output-rerun:${issue_num} -->

   _Standalone stall recovery: this issue has been in `ai:clarification` for ${elapsed_minutes}m with no clarification output. Re-running clarification once; if it still produces nothing, the issue is escalated to a human._
   ```
   - The marker must be the second line exactly, so the `startswith` check matches.
   - Everything else in the arm stays the same: `phase_cap_note_dispatch "ai:clarification"`, the DEBUG Telegram alert, and increment / took_action set to true.
   - The no-labels body stays byte-identical.

4. **Held advisory in the security-dependency hold branch** (about lines 24948-24955). After the existing unchanged `STALL_SKIP ... reason=security_dependency_held detail=...` echo and before `continue`, call a new helper `_post_security_dependency_held_advisory "${issue_num}" "${_security_dependency_verdict}" "${_security_dependency_status}" "${comments_json}" "${_standalone_staged_support_cache_available}"`.
   - **Read the dependency.** Take `depends_on` from the verdict and validate it against `^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$`. If it is missing or invalid, log `action=advisory_no_dependency` and return 0.
   - **Check the history is complete.** It is complete when cache is `true` with fewer than 100 comments, or when cache is `complete`. If not, log `action=advisory_comments_incomplete` and post nothing. There is no extra fetch, as AD-2 requires.
   - **Deduplicate.** If any trusted comment (same trust list) contains `<!-- ai:security-dependency-held:<issue>:<depends_on> -->`, log `action=advisory_present`.
   - **Post.** Otherwise make one `gh_retry gh api .../comments -f body=...` call, then log `action=advisory_posted` or `action=advisory_failed`. The body depends on the detail:
     - `open`: the issue waits for #M (the earlier fix to the same file) to be closed with `ai:merged`. Clarification then starts automatically. No action is needed.
     - `closed_without_ai_merged`: #M was closed without `ai:merged`, so this hold will not release on its own. A maintainer must act: land the prerequisite fix, or edit this issue's `- Depends on: #M` line.
     - `unverified`: the dependency on #M could not be verified, so this hold will not release on its own. A maintainer must act in the same way.
   - The marker goes on the last line. The body never has a line starting `/reclarify` or `/answer`, and never contains `<!-- ai:clarification-questions -->`.
   - Log line shape: `STALL_SKIP issue=N reason=security_dependency_held_advisory depends_on=<M|none> detail=<D> action=<...>`.
   - The helper always returns 0, so a failure never stops the loop.

5. **`agents.d/9486-clarify-no-output-rerun.md`**: one block under `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`. It documents both behaviours, both markers, the new `STALL_SKIP` / `STALL_RECOVERY` reason values (these are existing prefixes, so the log-prefix registry gets no new entry), the trust list, and the tests.

6. **`changelog.d/9486-clarify-no-output-rerun.md`**: a short user-facing entry in the same format as the existing fragments.

## Data structures affected
- No change to the `AI_STANDALONE_STALL_STATE_V1` schema. The `/reclarify` marker comment is the durable record of the first miss; `stall_recovery_count` still increments through the existing arm.
- Two new comment markers: `<!-- ai:clarify-no-output-rerun:<issue> -->` and `<!-- ai:security-dependency-held:<issue>:<depends_on> -->`.
- No changes to `orchestrate_lib.py` ladders, `VALID_STALL_RECOVERY_ACTIONS` or priorities. Only the existing `retrigger_pipeline` and `escalate
